messages:
sarah: Heads up — onboarding a customer where Key Vault lives in tenant-A but their app identity is in tenant-B. Can we sketch options for managed identity / cross-tenant access and what we should avoid?

mike: short answer: user-assigned/managed identities can't be used across AAD tenants directly. you'll need either a service principal in the vault's tenant, a guest/spn via B2B, or an app registration that is multi-tenant with consent.

julia: +1. Also we need to pick whether we use RBAC or access policies on the vault. RBAC is newer and maps well to AAD roles ("Key Vault Secrets User", "Key Vault Crypto User"). Access policies are older but still in use for some flows.

ken: for cross-tenant scenarios i've done: create an app registration in tenant-B (multi-tenant), then admin-consent in tenant-A, then grant the app the needed role on the KV resource via RBAC. avoids storing client secrets if we use federated credentials.

sarah: federated creds — do we mean workload identity federation (OIDC) for GitHub/AKS? or Azure federated credentials for service principals? need concrete steps.

mike: i mean the new AAD federated credential on the app (subject from workload), but that still requires an app/service principal object in the KV tenant. two paths: 1) create service principal in tenant-A and issue client secret/cert to the app in tenant-B (classic), or 2) make the app multi-tenant and get admin consent in tenant-A so its SP appears there and you can role-assign. path 2 is cleaner for short-lived creds.

julia: important security notes: enable purge protection + soft-delete on KV. enable diagnostic logs to our LA/workspace (AuditEvent). don't rely on client-side key caching for rotated keys.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: When you enable diagnostics on a Key Vault, please ensure retention policy and workspace are set. Example CLI to push AuditEvent logs: ```az monitor diagnostic-settings create --name kv-audit --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/<workspace> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'```

ken: role names to consider: "Key Vault Secrets User" (read secrets), "Key Vault Crypto User" (wrap/unwrap, sign), and "Key Vault Administrator" (management). If using RBAC, grant the least privilege role.

sarah: operational question: how do we rotate keys/certs without downtime when the vault is in another tenant? thoughts on envelope encryption and DEKs?

mike: Use envelope encryption: app encrypts data with a DEK (symmetric key) and DEK is protected by KV key. For rotation: create new KEK version in KV and update DEK-wrapping to use new version. keep fallback to old version until all consumers re-wrap. track version in metadata.

julia: also consider a short rewrap job that pulls wrapped DEKs, unwraps with old key, rewraps with new key. do it in batches and add a migration flag.

sec-oncall: incident note — if cross-tenant auth fails we get 401s from AKV and AuditEvent shows "AuthorizationFailed" in logs. set an alert on that log pattern. also confirm conditional access policies in tenant-A won't block SP logins from tenant-B.

sarah: action items: 1) infra to validate multi-tenant app flow and create admin-consent checklist. 2) sec to document RBAC vs access policy recommendations + roles. 3) eng to prototype rewrap job for DEKs. Assigning: @ken for infra, @julia for sec docs, @mike for prototype.

ken: i'll start with a small test app and share CLI steps. posted snippet i'll use for role assignment: ```# create sp in tenant-A (if needed) az ad sp create --id <appId> --tenant <tenantA> # role assign az role assignment create --assignee <spObjectId> --role "Key Vault Secrets User" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>```

mike: thanks. if anyone runs into MFA/consent issues in tenant-A ping me, we've had to ask tenant admins to enable "Users can consent to apps" or do explicit admin consent.

sarah: great thread — i'll capture this in the onboarding doc and link the test steps once ken posts them. :thumbsup:
